question: Should Telegram expose standalone `pin` and `unpin` message-tool actions, and what gate plus target semantics should protect them?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing pin/unpin lets agents change persistent chat state through privileged bot credentials, and the existing config surface has no pin-specific gate or approved implicit-unpin contract.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit action gate, require a concrete `messageId` unless maintainers approve an implicit mode, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Do not expose standalone pin/unpin actions yet; keep the existing delivery-pin capability for messages OpenClaw just sent.

options.title: Request a narrower design first
options.body: Ask for a small design note covering admin-right expectations, per-account gating, implicit unpin behavior, and forum-topic semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit action gate, require a concrete `messageId` unless maintainers approve an implicit mode, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the Telegram message-tool discovery and action-runtime ownership boundary this decision would extend.
